## Rough Draft Oaks Project Analysis

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

## Loading packages

First, we will load the packages needed for this analysis.

```{r}
library(readxl)
library(tidyverse)
```

The `echo: false` option disables the printing of code (only output is displayed).

## Summary table

Next, we will load in our datasets:

```{r}
# The following code was written by Amy King-Henry:
Moist_Data_Raw <- 
  read_excel("Oak Data Entry MCRS Field Trip.xlsx", 
             sheet = "Soil Moisture")

LICOR_Data_Raw_NAMES <- 
  read_excel("Oak Data Entry MCRS Field Trip.xlsx",              
             sheet = "LICOR", 
             n_max = 3, 
             col_names = FALSE, 
             col_types = "text") |> 
  summarise(across(.fns = paste, collapse = "_")) |> 
  unlist() |> 
  unname()

LICOR_Data_Raw <- 
  read_excel("Oak Data Entry MCRS Field Trip.xlsx",  
             sheet = "LICOR", 
             skip = 3, 
             col_names = LICOR_Data_Raw_NAMES,
             col_types = "text")


ALL_Licor_NAMES <- 
  read_excel("Oak Data Entry MCRS Field Trip.xlsx", 
             sheet = "ALL_Licor_Ignore", 
             n_max = 3, 
             col_names = FALSE, 
             col_types = "text") |> 
  summarise(across(.fns = paste, collapse = "_")) |> 
  unlist() |> 
  unname()

ALL_Licor <- 
  read_excel("Oak Data Entry MCRS Field Trip.xlsx", 
             sheet = "ALL_Licor_Ignore", 
             skip = 3, 
             col_names = ALL_Licor_NAMES, 
             col_types = "text")

LICOR_Data_Raw <- full_join(LICOR_Data_Raw, ALL_Licor)

# Everything above this was code written by Amy King-Henry
# From here, modifications to the LICOR and 

Moist_Data_Raw

head(Moist_Data_Raw)

#Moist_Data_Clean <- Moist_Data_Raw |> 
#drop_na(Treatment)

# Natural recruits were found across all treatments, not relevant for the possible differences between microhabitats
Moist_Data_Clean <- Moist_Data_Raw |> 
  filter(Treatment != "NR")

# Making the date the same as data sets used later
Moist_Data_Clean$Date <- as.character(Moist_Data_Clean$Date)
head(Moist_Data_Clean)

Moist_Data_Clean <- Moist_Data_Clean |>
  mutate(VWC1_perc = as.numeric(VWC1_perc))

Moist_Data_Clean <- Moist_Data_Clean |>
  mutate(VWC2_perc = as.numeric(VWC2_perc))

Moist_Data_Clean <- Moist_Data_Clean |>
  mutate(VWC3_perc = as.numeric(VWC3_perc))

Moist_Data_Clean <- Moist_Data_Clean |> 
  group_by(Block, Treatment, VWC1_perc, VWC2_perc, VWC3_perc)|>
  mutate(VWC_avg = mean(c(VWC1_perc, VWC2_perc, VWC3_perc), na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  ungroup()

Moist_Data_Clean

LICOR_Data_Raw

LICOR_Data_Clean <- LICOR_Data_Raw |>
  rename(Date = SYS_Date_YYYYMMDD)

LICOR_Data_Clean <- LICOR_Data_Clean |>
  rename(Block = 'USERDEF_Block Number_NA')

LICOR_Data_Clean <- LICOR_Data_Clean |>
  rename(Treatment = Treatment_NA_NA)

LICOR_Data_Clean <- LICOR_Data_Clean |>
  rename(Tag_Number = 'USERDEF_Tag Number_NA')

LICOR_Data_Clean <- LICOR_Data_Clean |>
  rename(Transpiration = `PORO_E_apparent_mmol+1m-2s-1`)

head(LICOR_Data_Clean)

LICOR_Data_Clean <- LICOR_Data_Clean |>
  mutate(Transpiration = as.numeric(Transpiration))

LICOR_Data_Clean

LICOR_Transpiration <- LICOR_Data_Clean |> 
  drop_na(Transpiration)

LICOR_Transpiration <- LICOR_Transpiration |> 
  drop_na(Treatment)

LICOR_Transpiration <- LICOR_Transpiration |>
  filter(Treatment != 'NR')

LICOR_Transpiration <- LICOR_Transpiration |>
  filter(Treatment != '??')

LICOR_Transpiration <- LICOR_Transpiration |> 
  group_by(Tag_Number, Treatment, Block)|>
  summarize(Transpiration_avg = mean(Transpiration, na.rm = TRUE))

LICOR_Transpiration
```
